extracted.intended_audience: local government communicators, municipal administrators, public safety officers, and emergency management staff
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for building an actionable emergency/crisis communication plan for local governments, covering audience identification, channels, coordination with safety officials, staffing/infrastructure, social media strategy, team preparedness, and message crafting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Start by Identifying Your Audiences
rubrics_metrics.description: While your immediate concern is likely for the safety of your citizens, start your crisis communication planning by identifying all the audiences that you will need to communicate with if a disaster occurs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List should include Citizens (triage by proximity to incident), Visitors (non-residents in area), Local Businesses (impact, role in recovery), and The Media (local/regional outlets; include media contacts and shortlist of trained spokespeople). Triage communications to affected populations rather than broadcasting to everyone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citizens (audience triage)
rubrics_metrics.description: Think about triaging communication to residents based on their proximity to the incident.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: You may not need to communicate with all citizens in your county about a water main break, but you should communicate to everyone in and traveling to the immediate area.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visitors (reach non-residents)
rubrics_metrics.description: Don’t forget non-residents who happen to be in the area when a disaster strikes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They are at risk and may not have opted into local alerts—plan specific channels (media, digital road signs) to reach them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local Businesses (stakeholder communications)
rubrics_metrics.description: Local disasters may have specific consequences for businesses in your community who play essential roles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inform businesses how events impact operations and the role they can play in managing the crisis and recovery.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Media (establish media contacts and spokespeople)
rubrics_metrics.description: Your local and regional media outlets will want to know what events have occurred and your administration’s plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include media contacts in your plan; create a shortlist of trained administration members who can speak directly with the media and receive advanced crisis communication training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Build Contact Lists and Establish Communication Channels in Advance
rubrics_metrics.description: When a disaster occurs, it’s already too late to try to obtain contact information for all audiences—start preparing now by encouraging citizens to opt-in to receive emergency alerts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a government emergency notification system to accept opt-ins and distribute alerts to multiple channels (SMS/text, email, voice). Pre-build contact lists for stakeholders and media.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make Sure You Have a Way to Reach Visitors
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a strategy for reaching visitors in the area—non-residents who wouldn’t have signed up to receive emergency alerts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use local media, digital road signs, and an emergency warning system that can reach non-opted-in devices (see IPAWS integration).

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrate with IPAWS (FEMA Integrated Public Alert Warning System)
rubrics_metrics.description: If you implement an emergency warning system, choose a solution that integrates with IPAWS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IPAWS can send notifications to all cell phones within a specified area without delay from congestion, interrupt local TV/radio broadcasts, and post to digital road signs and other locations instantaneously.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate Planning Efforts with Safety Officials
rubrics_metrics.description: Include contact information for local public safety officials and a strategy for who is responsible for communicating with them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work with safety officials in advance to co-create protocols and procedures for delivering vital safety information and instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish Infrastructure and Training for Communication Triage
rubrics_metrics.description: After audiences and channels are planned, put together a communication triage strategy detailing staffing, processes, and tools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include call center plans, web publishing responsibilities, internal comms, and fallback connectivity options to ensure sustained communications during disruptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Call center staffing
rubrics_metrics.description: Expect higher than average call volume from all audiences during a crisis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan to staff the call center accordingly or redirect incoming calls to a second call center if possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure key staff is trained in updating your local government website
rubrics_metrics.description: Your municipal website will be one of the first places people go to find the latest information regarding the disaster.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Train key members on how/where to publish emergency alerts; use a CMS that allows publishing from mobile devices and is not cumbersome during emergencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure that you have an internal communication strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Don’t overlook the importance of building a plan for internal stakeholders to communicate with one another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Local government administrators need to alert and convene key personnel instantly; plan for implementation even if cell service is disrupted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrated conference bridge / ability to convene decision-makers quickly
rubrics_metrics.description: A valuable emergency notification system will include an integrated conference bridge to connect decision-makers on a unified call.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This enables time-sensitive next-step planning within seconds during crises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include Social Media in Your Multi-Channel Communication Strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Social media is a critical channel for delivering real-time urgent news and emergency notifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Citizens expect breaking news on social platforms; social media breaks news fast, crosses boundaries, and is watched by journalists—use it to share reliable, actionable information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key Platforms — Facebook
rubrics_metrics.description: Facebook is potentially the most impactful social network for citizens; it supports text, images, maps, links, downloadable content, and safety features.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use your government Facebook as a source of reliable news, instructions, resources, and to leverage features like family locator and 'mark as safe'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key Platforms — X (formerly Twitter)
rubrics_metrics.description: Twitter users are likely to comment on or react to breaking news; it often serves as an echo chamber.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect commentary and rapid spread; monitor and correct misinformation; use it for rapid updates and engagement with active users and journalists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create Guidelines (team policies and protocols)
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop messaging and channel-specific content guidelines, policies, and protocols for all staff who will assist with communications before an event occurs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document what to post when, who approves messages, and rules for verification and tone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Build a Team
rubrics_metrics.description: Have a plan for a small team to assist during a crisis, not just one person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign roles: one to post updates, one to answer public/media questions, one to fact-check and correct rumors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct System Training Now
rubrics_metrics.description: Familiarize your team with social platforms, social listening, and mass notification tools before a disaster occurs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practice using platforms and tools so staff can act quickly when a real event occurs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborate with emergency response partners
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish partnerships with local and national emergency response teams to share information and coordinate communications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Joint communications can spread messages more widely and reinforce trusted sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Craft Templates in Advance
rubrics_metrics.description: Create pre-written communication messages for possible emergency events that can be distributed quickly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a mass notification solution that offers templated messages to speed distribution during events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Utilize a Government Content Management System (CMS)
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose a website solution with an integrated emergency warning system that allows cross-channel posting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer CMS with integrated emergency functionality to send critical communications to all social channels in a single step.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure Mobile Capabilities for Administrators
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a CMS and tools that enable crafting and sending messages from a mobile device.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emergencies can occur anytime; ensure administrators can operate tools while away from office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess (post-event review)
rubrics_metrics.description: When the crisis and immediate recovery period have ended, take time to assess what went well and where you can improve.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct after-action review to update plans, templates, staffing, and tech choices for future events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure Multilingual Translation Capabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: If a significant portion of your citizens are non-English speakers, ensure tools enable citizens to consume content in their preferred language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Have translation workflows and technology ready to provide critical information in multiple languages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be Accurate.
rubrics_metrics.description: The most important thing is to release the correct information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if it means a short delay, validate sources and avoid errors or inconsistencies in messaging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep Messages Short and Actionable.
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not overwhelm readers with superfluous details; focus on the most critical information and provide succinct, actionable instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Link to detailed content (evacuation maps, shelter lists) rather than packing all details into one message.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be Specific.
rubrics_metrics.description: Give citizens specific feedback, such as location of shelters or road closures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid vague statements; provide concrete, location-based, and time-sensitive instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stay Calm and Carry On (tone)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure the tone of all communications is calm and informative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid alarmist language; authoritative, composed messaging helps maintain public trust and reduces panic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leverage Hashtags.
rubrics_metrics.description: On social media, include hashtags to amplify the reach of your message to non-followers (e.g., #HurricaneMartha).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use consistent, event-specific hashtags to make updates discoverable and to aggregate information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Share Trusted Resources.
rubrics_metrics.description: Share and repost updates from other trusted organizational partners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amplify credible partners to provide comprehensive information and reinforce trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review Scheduled Communications.
rubrics_metrics.description: Turn off scheduled social media posts and emails that may be out of sync with the unexpected disaster.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scheduled non-emergency messages (e.g., parade announcements) can appear out-of-place and undermine credibility during a crisis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Send Updates Frequently.
rubrics_metrics.description: Citizens will be looking for continual updates, so keep emails, tweets, posts, and news releases of valuable news and instruction coming frequently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frequent updates maintain situational awareness and public confidence; balance frequency with accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Share Updates Consistently.
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the same messaging strategy across all communication channels to mitigate mixed messages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate wording, timing, and key facts across platforms and spokespeople to avoid contradictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stay Vigilant (monitor and respond)
rubrics_metrics.description: Continually monitor news, third-party media outlets, and social media to stay in contact with impacted residents and maintain awareness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use social listening to identify rumors and needs; correct misinformation promptly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continue Communicating Through the Recovery Period.
rubrics_metrics.description: Continue to share updates even when an event has ended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide information on recovery, clean-up progress, and available resources—citizens remain interested after the immediate crisis.
